conditions.label: Complete placenta previa with hemorrhage, second trimester

reports.text:
Indication: 20w0d by LMP and first-trimester ultrasound; anatomy survey; one week of light painless spotting.
Single intrauterine pregnancy, cephalic. Fetal cardiac activity present, heart rate 148 bpm. Biometry concordant with dates; estimated fetal weight appropriate for gestational age. Amniotic fluid normal.
Placenta: posterior, extending across and completely covering the internal cervical os on transabdominal and transvaginal views. No retroplacental collection. No sonographic features of abnormal placental adherence.
Fetal anatomy: head, face, spine, heart (four-chamber view and outflow tracts), stomach, kidneys, bladder, abdominal wall, cord insertion and extremities seen and normal. Three-vessel cord.
Cervix closed.
reports.conclusion: Complete placenta previa. Single live intrauterine pregnancy at 20 weeks with normal anatomy and appropriate growth. Recommend follow-up transvaginal ultrasound at about 32 weeks.

documents.title: Obstetrics - Prenatal Visit 20 Weeks
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
RE: Alyssa Krause, DOB 11/30/1992
Visit date: 1/13/2026, 20w0d

Dear colleague,

Your patient came in for her scheduled 20-week visit. She is doing well overall. For about a week she has had light spotting on and off, never painful, no cramping, no contractions. Until now this pregnancy has gone smoothly, with normal blood pressures and no diabetes. She asked about delivery planning and would like to deliver vaginally again, as she did with her first two.

Vitals stable. Fetal heart rate regular at 148. We did not do a pelvic or digital exam given the bleeding.

She went straight to ultrasound for her anatomy scan, which shows a complete placenta previa, posterior placenta fully covering the internal os. Anatomy is normal and growth is on track. Report enclosed.

We explained that many low placentas move up as the uterus grows, but a placenta that is still covering the os later in pregnancy means a cesarean birth, and she understands vaginal delivery may not be possible. Pelvic rest, nothing in the vagina, and she knows to come to Labor & Delivery right away for any bleeding heavier than spotting, contractions or pain. Repeat transvaginal ultrasound around 32 weeks.

Medications: prenatal vitamin. Allergies: NKDA.

Sincerely,
Obstetrics & Gynecology

events.reason: Question about work with placenta previa

documents.title: Placenta previa and work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, just wanted you to know my OB found a placenta previa at my 20 week scan. Baby looks good otherwise. I've only had a little spotting and it stopped a few days ago. I'm on my feet all day with 7 year olds - is that OK? OB said pelvic rest but didn't say anything about work.

documents.title: RE: Placenta previa and work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know, I saw their letter. Glad the spotting has settled. Standing and normal activity at school are generally fine with a previa as long as you feel well; it's the pelvic rest and getting checked quickly for any bleeding that matter most. Your OB team calls the shots on activity, so ask them at your next visit if they want any limits, and if they write a work note we can help with paperwork.

conditions.label: Severe fetal anemia due to fetomaternal hemorrhage, third trimester

documents.title: Antepartum Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
ANTEPARTUM DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Patient: Alyssa Krause   DOB 11/30/1992
Admitted 3/26/2026 via Labor & Delivery triage   Discharged 3/29/2026
Service: Obstetrics / Maternal-Fetal Medicine

Admission diagnosis: decreased fetal movement, IUP at 30w2d
Discharge diagnoses: severe fetal anemia secondary to fetomaternal hemorrhage, s/p intrauterine transfusion; complete placenta previa without bleeding

History: 33 yo G3P2002 at 30w2d (EDD 6/2/2026) with a known complete previa presented after six hours of noticeably fewer movements. No bleeding, no fluid, no contractions. Meds: prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Course: Maternal vitals normal. NST nonreactive with minimal variability. Ultrasound: no hydrops; MCA peak systolic velocity 1.82 MoM; complete placenta previa persists, no retroplacental collection. Maternal Kleihauer-Betke 2.4% fetal cells, estimated fetomaternal hemorrhage about 120 mL fetal whole blood. Maternal CBC normal. Blood type A positive, antibody screen negative; no Rh immune globulin indicated.

Betamethasone 12 mg IM given 3/26 and 3/27. Intrauterine transfusion by cordocentesis 3/26 with irradiated, CMV-negative O-negative red cells: fetal hemoglobin 5.6 g/dL before, 13.9 g/dL after. No procedural complications. NST reactive by the next day; MCA-PSV 1.10 MoM on 3/27. Fetal movement back to her usual. No bleeding throughout the stay.

Discharge plan: MCA Doppler and NST twice weekly at MFM; repeat transfusion if MCA-PSV rises above 1.5 MoM. Planned cesarean at 36w3d (5/8/2026) for the previa unless needed sooner. Previa precautions unchanged. Return at once for bleeding, contractions or decreased movement. Off work from today; leave paperwork through our office.

Discharge medications: prenatal vitamin 1 tablet daily.
Follow-up: MFM 3/31; primary care as needed.

documents.title: Leave Paperwork
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called. School district sent her leave forms and she wasn't sure who fills them out. Per hospital discharge summary her OB office is handling pregnancy leave. Gave her the OB office fax and she will send them there. Pt also asked to keep her 4/8 appt with PCP for now.

documents.title: Maternal-Fetal Medicine - Antepartum Update
documents.author: maternal-fetal medicine
documents.body:
RE: Alyssa Krause, DOB 11/30/1992
Update at 32w3d

Dear colleague,

A brief update on our shared patient since her intrauterine transfusion on 3/26.

She has come in twice a week for MCA Dopplers and NSTs. Every MCA-PSV since the transfusion has been below 1.5 MoM and every NST has been reactive, so no second transfusion has been needed. She reports good movements. No bleeding. The placenta remains a complete previa on this week's transvaginal scan.

For your records: her 1-hour glucose screen at 26 weeks (2/24) was normal, and she received Tdap on 3/10 at 28 weeks.

Cesarean is still planned for 5/8/2026 at 36w3d. Surveillance continues twice weekly until then.

Medications: prenatal vitamin. Allergies: NKDA.

Maternal-Fetal Medicine

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRIC DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Patient: Alyssa Krause   DOB 11/30/1992
Admitted 5/5/2026   Discharged 5/8/2026
Service: Obstetrics

Admission diagnosis: absent fetal movement, IUP at 36w0d
Discharge diagnoses: intrauterine fetal demise at 36w0d; complete placenta previa; history of severe fetal anemia from fetomaternal hemorrhage s/p intrauterine transfusion 3/26/2026; s/p primary low transverse cesarean delivery

History: 33 yo G3P2002 followed closely at MFM after her March transfusion, with a cesarean planned for 5/8. She came to Labor & Delivery in the morning, having last felt the baby move the evening before. No bleeding, no loss of fluid, no abdominal pain.

Exam: vitals stable. Fundal height consistent with dates. Fetal heart tones could not be found with the Doppler. Bedside ultrasound showed no fetal cardiac activity; confirmed by a second examiner.

We talked with Alyssa and her husband at length. Because of the complete previa, vaginal delivery was not an option. Primary low transverse cesarean under spinal anesthesia was done that evening, 5/5/2026 at 19:12. Stillborn female, 2,380 g. Estimated blood loss 900 mL; no transfusion. The family spent time with their daughter, and perinatal social work and the bereavement team met with them.

Stillbirth evaluation: repeat maternal Kleihauer-Betke 1.3% fetal cells. Placenta sent for pathology. Autopsy and genetic testing were offered and declined.

Postpartum course: afebrile, pain controlled with oral medication, ambulating, tolerating diet, voiding. Hemoglobin 10.2 g/dL on POD1. Incision clean. Lactation suppression discussed; supportive measures only (supportive bra, cold packs, avoid stimulation).

Discharge medications:
- ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours as needed with food
- acetaminophen 1,000 mg every 6 hours as needed
- prenatal vitamin 1 tablet daily

Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: OB postpartum visit at 6 weeks; placental pathology to be reviewed then. Primary care within 2 weeks. Bereavement resources given.

documents.title: PCP Call After Discharge
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Read the discharge summary this morning and called Alyssa. Told her how very sorry I am. She is home since Friday, husband home with her. Pain is manageable with ibuprofen and acetaminophen, using less each day. Incision ok, no redness or drainage, no fever. Bleeding like a period and lighter. Breasts sore but settling with what L&D suggested. Not sleeping much. Eating some.

No thoughts of hurting herself. Knows she can call or text me any time.

Plan: visit next week, ~2 wks after surgery. Reviewed when to call OB: fever, heavy bleeding, wound changes, calf pain or SOB.

documents.title: Office Visit - Post Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
33 yo G3P2102, here 15 days after primary cesarean for intrauterine fetal demise at 36 weeks (5/5). Pregnancy was complicated by complete placenta previa found at 20 wks and severe fetal anemia from fetomaternal hemorrhage at 30 wks, treated with an intrauterine transfusion; she had been on twice-weekly monitoring with surgery planned for 5/8. Discharge summary reviewed. Hgb 10.2 POD1. Placental pathology pending; autopsy and genetics declined.

She came alone. Cried on and off talking about her daughter, which seems right. Family close by and her husband is home through the end of the month. Sleeping 4-5 hours, wakes and can't get back down. Appetite coming back. Two older kids keeping her going. Still on leave from school.

Physically: incision a little tender, no drainage. Lochia light. Milk has mostly stopped. Only taking ibuprofen at night now. Some fatigue climbing stairs. No fever, no calf pain, no SOB.

Meds: prenatal vitamin daily; ibuprofen prn.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Tired, appropriately tearful, engaged. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, Pfannenstiel incision intact, healing well, no erythema or induration. Calves soft, nontender.

PHQ-9 4, mostly sleep and energy. Denies hopelessness, no SI.

A/P
1. Recent stillbirth and cesarean. Recovering as expected. Grief, not depression right now. Gave her the perinatal loss support group information from L&D again plus a local one that meets evenings. Will keep checking in; PHQ-9 each visit.
2. Post-op fatigue with Hgb 10.2. Recheck CBC in about a month.
3. OB postpartum visit 6/16 is booked.

TCM: contact within 2 business days of discharge (5/11), face-to-face within 14 days, moderate complexity.

RTC 6-8 wks or sooner.

reports.text:
Specimen: placenta, singleton, third trimester, with umbilical cord and membranes.
Gross: trimmed placental disc 470 g. Three-vessel umbilical cord with central insertion. Membranes translucent, complete. Maternal surface intact; no adherent clot. Serial sections without infarct or mass.
Microscopic: villous maturation appropriate for gestational age. Fetal villous capillaries contain increased nucleated red blood cells. Villous edema present. No villitis, no chorioamnionitis, no funisitis. No infarction or decidual vasculopathy. No retroplacental hematoma.
reports.conclusion: Third-trimester placenta with increased circulating fetal nucleated red blood cells and villous edema, consistent with fetomaternal hemorrhage. No infarction, abruption or acute inflammation.

documents.title: Obstetrics - Postpartum Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
RE: Alyssa Krause, DOB 11/30/1992
Visit date: 6/16/2026

Dear colleague,

Mrs. Krause was seen six weeks after her cesarean delivery on 5/5 for a stillbirth at 36 weeks.

She is recovering physically. Incision is well healed. Bleeding stopped about two weeks ago. No breast concerns. She is grieving and has gone to one support group meeting. EPDS 8.

We went over the placental pathology, which shows changes consistent with fetomaternal hemorrhage and nothing else. Autopsy and genetic testing were declined. We told her that a hemorrhage like this one is unlikely to happen again, and that a future pregnancy would start with early care at MFM. After a cesarean we recommend waiting at least 18 months before conceiving. She and her husband will use condoms for now and do not want a hormonal method at this time.

Cleared for all activity, including returning to teaching. She plans to go back at the start of the school year.

Medications: prenatal vitamin. Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up with us for routine gynecologic care, or sooner if she is planning another pregnancy.

Sincerely,
Obstetrics & Gynecology
